3D Gaussian Splatting (3D-GS) was introduced by Kerbl et al. in 2023 [KKLD23] as an efficient explicit scene representation that achieves real-time rendering.
It departed from implicit MLP-based representations like NeRFs by using 3D Gaussians as graphical primitives.
The method optimizes a set of 3D Gaussians from a set of calibrated images to represent the scene.
The projection and rasterization steps described here are central to the 3D-GS pipeline, allowing for differentiable rendering and efficient gradient-based optimization.
